emma (ACME): Hi, we started seeing a bunch of 429s around 16:20 UTC for a short burst. Our dashboard shows we still had burst credits left (~18) so not sure why requests were blocked. Any quick pointers? :confused:
maggie-support: Sorry — can you paste the request id / sample response headers? 429 body + headers help a lot.
emma (ACME): Sample 429 body: `{\"error\":\"rate_limited\", \"message\":\"Quota exceeded\"}`. Headers:
```
X-Request-ID: r-9f3a2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1672500000
X-RateLimit-BurstCredits: 18
```
maggie-support: Interesting — header shows burst credits >0. Two quick checks: 1) were these requests hitting multiple model routes? 2) do you have any client-side retry/debounce?
emma (ACME): It's all one route (/v1/generate) but we do fan-out from a web worker when page loads — could be some client retry.
sanjay-infra: Paging in the infra signal: when many concurrent connections arrive within a tiny window, the platform applies a short debounce window to protect single-tenant capacity. That can cause immediate 429s even if burst credits exist, because credits are consumed at the per-second granularity.
ben-ops: To add — burst credits are a smoothing buffer, not an unlimited reserve. If many requests landed within the same token-generation epoch we may have exhausted the per-second throughput before credits are debited, triggering throttling.
maggie-support: Can you repro with a curl script? If you can capture `X-RateLimit-*` and `x-rw-usage` headers for a failing run that helps. Example repro: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"max_tokens\":16}' &
done; wait
```
sanjay-infra: Also check the `x-rw-debounce` header in responses — it indicates the short protective window. If present, it means requests were rate-limited by smoothing logic.
emma (ACME): Ran the script. Failures show `X-RateLimit-BurstCredits: 3` then `0` and `x-rw-debounce: 150ms`.
maggie-support: Thanks — that's our smoking gun. Smoothing set to 150ms means we intentionally hold a tiny cooldown to avoid tail-latency spikes across the pool. It can cause transient 429s during very tight fan-out.
ben-ops: Workarounds: 1) add client-side jitter + exponential backoff on 429s; 2) limit simultaneous inflight requests (concurrency cap); 3) request a temporary Dedicated or burst raise if traffic pattern is expected.
maggie-support: I'll open an internal follow-up with infra to see if we can tune debounce for your org (non-default). @sanjay-infra can you check whether ACME is eligible for a 2x smoothing window increase?
sanjay-infra: Yep, I can check. Also will add a note to docs: difference between \"burst credits\" (cumulative buffer) and \"debounce/smoothing\" (protective per-window throttle).
emma (ACME): Great, thanks — we'll add client-side backoff as a quick fix. Appreciate the explanation! :heart:
ratebot: Incident FYI: created ticket #INC-2022-781 for smoothing config review (assigned sanjay-infra).
